problem: The lead says "HTTP can carry only text" and uses that as the reason forms become name=value pairs. HTTP bodies carry arbitrary bytes; a file upload sends binary. The real reason is the HTML form data model is text: controls hold string values.
fix: Replace with: "A form's data model is text, so the browser flattens the form into pairs of name=value, joins them with &, and ships them either in the URL (GET) or in the request body (POST). File contents are the exception; they travel as multipart parts."

problem: "any character outside plain ASCII becomes a percent sign plus two hex digits" is wrong per character. The character is first encoded as UTF-8 bytes, and each byte becomes one %XX triplet. A rupee sign becomes three triplets, not one.
fix: "a space becomes %20 or +; any other character outside plain ASCII is first written as UTF-8 bytes and each byte becomes a percent sign plus two hex digits, so a rupee sign travels as %E2%82%B9 and a Tamil letter as three such triplets."

problem: "value — the value sent when the user changes nothing" is misleading. In a text field the value attribute is the default text, and anything the user types is sent instead; in a radio or checkbox it is the value sent when the control is checked, not a fallback for an untouched field.
fix: "value — the control's default value: the starting text of a text field (overridden by typing), or the value a radio or checkbox sends when it is chosen. A select keeps its values on its option elements."

problem: "required — the form cannot be sent while the field is empty" does not cover checkboxes and radio groups, where the condition is not emptiness but not being checked or chosen.
fix: "required — the form cannot be sent while the field has no value: an empty text box, a checkbox not ticked, or no radio in the group chosen."

problem: datalist is described as attaching to "a text input" only. The list attribute works on several input types, including search, url, email, tel, number, range and color.
fix: "datalist attaches suggestions to an input through list="id" (usually a text input, but also search, email, url, tel, number, range or color); the user may pick a suggestion or type something else, and whatever is in the box is sent."

problem: "checkbox for many of many" is unclear wording; a reader cannot tell what is being chosen from what.
fix: "checkbox for choosing any number of options from a list, each ticked box sending its own name=value pair."
